Definition: Areas where the dominant vegetative cover is below two metres in height and woody canopy cover is less than 20%.
Areas with less than 4% vegetative cover that do not have an artificial cover from human activities.
Areas that are covered by water, either naturally or artificially for more than 9 months of the year.
Areas that are covered by water, either naturally or artificially for less than or equal to 9 months of the year.
Areas where the natural vegetation has been removed or modified and replaced by other types of vegetative cover due to human activity.
Examples: Wheat, potato and tomato crops, and grazed pastures

Definition: Areas where the vegetative cover is at least two metres in height and has at least 20% canopy cover. These areas would be dominated by shrubs and trees.
Areas that have an artificial cover as a result of human activities.
Examples: Cities, towns, transportation, open mines, quarries and waste disposal
